items.question: Critically examine the extent to which the commitments made to Andhra Pradesh under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 have been fulfilled. What are the key pending issues?
items.modelAnswer:
The **AP Reorganisation Act, 2014** (appointed day 2 June 2014) not only bifurcated the State but also enumerated, chiefly in the **Thirteenth Schedule (s.93)** and **s.46/s.94**, a set of developmental commitments to compensate residuary Andhra Pradesh for the loss of **Hyderabad's revenue base** and its institutional infrastructure.

**Commitments substantially met:** Several **central institutions** promised for the 12th-13th Plan periods have been established — IIT Tirupati, IIM Visakhapatnam, IISER Tirupati and the Central University of Andhra Pradesh. The **new railway zone**, South Coast Railway with headquarters at Visakhapatnam, was **sanctioned in 2019**. The **Polavaram Irrigation Project** was declared a **national project (s.90)** and is under execution.

**Commitments unfulfilled or disputed:** The **Special Category Status** — a verbal assurance in the Rajya Sabha (Feb 2014) rather than a statutory guarantee — was **not granted**; after the 14th Finance Commission's approach, the Centre offered a **Special Package (2016)** instead, which AP regards as inadequate. The **Dugarajupatnam major port** was effectively dropped, the **Kadapa integrated steel plant** remains only partly realised, and **Polavaram funding** (2013-14 vs revised cost estimates) and R&R are locked in an AP-Centre dispute. **Revenue-deficit compensation** and the special development package for the **Rayalaseema and north-coastal regions (s.46)** remain contentious.

**Conclusion:** While institution-building has largely progressed, the **large-ticket infrastructure and fiscal commitments** are the sticking points. Fulfilment turns on Centre-State cooperative federalism, clear costing of Polavaram, and honouring the spirit — if not the letter — of the bifurcation assurances. Timely implementation is essential to address the structural handicap the residuary State inherited.
keyPoints: Act's commitments concentrated in the Thirteenth Schedule (s.93) plus s.46 (fiscal) and s.94.
Met: central institutions (IIT/IIM/IISER/Central Univ), South Coast Railway zone (2019), Polavaram declared national (s.90).
Unmet/disputed: SCS not granted (Special Package 2016 instead), Dugarajupatnam port dropped, Kadapa steel plant partial, Polavaram funding.
Fiscal: revenue-deficit grant (14th FC) and special package for Rayalaseema & north-coastal regions remain contentious.
Way forward: cooperative federalism, clear Polavaram costing, honouring bifurcation assurances.
items.source: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (s.46, s.90, s.93-94, Thirteenth Schedule); Special Package 2016; Ministry of Railways

items.question: Discuss the mechanisms provided under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 for sharing and managing Krishna and Godavari waters between the successor States, and the significance of the Polavaram project.
items.modelAnswer:
Water was among the most sensitive fault-lines of bifurcation, since both successor States are heavily dependent on the **Krishna and Godavari** basins. The Act therefore built a dedicated institutional architecture.

**River Management Boards (s.85):** The Act created the **Krishna River Management Board (KRMB)** and the **Godavari River Management Board (GRMB)** under the Union, to regulate and supervise releases and allocations. Their **headquarters were split — KRMB in Andhra Pradesh and GRMB in Telangana** — and they operate on the principles of the **Eleventh Schedule**, under which prior awards of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal are binding on both States.

**Tribunal and Tungabhadra (s.89, s.91):** The **term of the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal** was extended to adjudicate outstanding issues, and both successor States were substituted for the erstwhile State on the **Tungabhadra Board**, which continues to monitor the High Level Canal, Low Level Canal and Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme.

**Polavaram (s.90):** The **Polavaram Irrigation Project** on the Godavari was **declared a national project**, with the **Union taking control** of its development and Telangana's consent **deemed given**. It is central to AP's irrigation, drinking-water and hydropower needs and to the Godavari-Krishna link, making it the single most significant water commitment of the Act.

**Assessment:** The framework is sound in design but strained in practice — disputes over project appraisals, unauthorised projects, and Polavaram's funding and R&R persist. Effective, apolitical functioning of the Boards and clear Central financing are key to equitable water sharing.
keyPoints: Section 85 created KRMB and GRMB under the Union; KRMB HQ in AP, GRMB HQ in Telangana.
Eleventh Schedule principles govern the Boards; prior KWDT awards binding on both States.
Section 89 extended the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal term; s.91 put both States on the Tungabhadra Board.
Section 90 declared Polavaram (on the Godavari) a national project with the Union in control and Telangana's consent deemed.
Practice strained by project-appraisal disputes and Polavaram funding/R&R issues.
items.source: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (s.85, s.89, s.90, s.91, Eleventh Schedule)
